subject: Demo follow-up: pricing scenarios & prefix-store hit-rate models
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@finovate.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Demo follow-up: pricing scenarios & prefix-store hit-rate models

Thanks again for the time today, Alicia — great conversation and helpful context on how Finovate is using short, templated prompts across several product flows. Quick recap and a few concrete pricing scenarios to help you evaluate feasibility against your $/1M target.

TL;DR (recommendation):
- We can likely get your effective cost under $50 / 1M served tokens with a focused prefix-store strategy + 30–45% hit rate on the high-frequency prompts you demonstrated.
- Attached is an XLSX with three scenario rows (Conservative / Mid / Aggressive) that map hit rate -> effective $/1M -> estimated monthly spend for your stated volumes.

Recap of what you shared:
- Typical monthly delivered tokens (user-facing): ~60M (avg), spikes to ~120M during peak campaigns
- Key flows: identity verification prompts (high repeatability), customer-facing FAQs (moderate repeatability), free-text support (low repeatability)
- Budget: looking to peg effective cost under $40–$60 per 1M served tokens to get board signoff for an initial pilot

Pricing model assumptions I used (see attached workbook for calldata):
- Redwood hosted baseline model list price: $25 / 1M tokens processed by the model (this is the chargeable unit before caching)
- Effective cost to deliver 1M served tokens = base_price * (1 - hit_rate) when hits return the full response and bypass model compute
- Prefix-store hit: only reuses the leading N tokens / KV segments; on average we treat prefix hits as 0.6x the benefit of a full-response hit (i.e., a 30% prefix hit approximates a 18% full-response-equivalent hit for cost math)
- Operational TTL and storage costs are nominal at pilot scale and excluded from the simple per-1M math; we can include them if you'd like a full TCO breakdown

Three illustrative scenarios (rounded):
- Conservative: 10% effective full-response-equivalent hit -> effective $/1M = $25 * (1 - 0.10) = $22.50 -> monthly cost at 60M served = 60 * $22.50 = $1,350
- Mid: 30% -> effective $/1M = $17.50 -> monthly cost at 60M = $1,050
- Aggressive: 50% -> effective $/1M = $12.50 -> monthly cost at 60M = $750

Note on prefix-store translation: because many of your prompts are short template-driven prefixes, we modeled two layers in the workbook: prefix hit-rate (observed in request logs) and an equivalence factor that converts prefix hits into full-response-equivalent cost reduction. For example: 40% prefix hit * 0.6 equivalence = 24% effective hit in the table.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm a 90-day sample of request logs (anonymized) or a CSV export with token counts by prompt template so we can run a quick hit-rate sweep? (Ben can ingest and run the simulation.)
2) If you’re comfortable, Ben and I can spin up a short Proof-of-Concept with 2–3 high-frequency templates instrumented for prefix-store and report back measured hit rates after 2 weeks.
3) If the PoC aligns to the Mid scenario, we’ll draft a scoped pilot MSA and work with procurement on standard SLAs.

Attachments: pricing-scenarios-priyom-v1.xlsx (scenario tabs + assumptions), mutual-action-plan-Finovate.pdf (proposed pilot steps)

Thanks — happy to walk through any numbers in a short call next week.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@finovate.co>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: pricing scenarios & prefix-store hit-rate models

Thanks, Priyom — this is super helpful and the simple math makes sense. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Volumes: our current production averages roughly 60M served tokens / month (as you used) but we see predictable campaign spikes that double that for 3–5 days a month. For planning, assume sustained 60M with short spikes to 120M.
2) Template breakdown (by percentage of requests):
   - Identity & verification: ~28% (very high repeatability: same few prompts, short tokens)
   - Billing & FAQ: ~42% (moderate repeatability; many variants but same templates)
   - Free-text support / case creation: ~30% (low repeatability)
3) Budget: our procurement team has flagged a target effective ceiling of $50 / 1M served tokens for the pilot. If we can demonstrate sub-$40 with reasonable hit rates, we could accelerate to a 6-month contract.

I can share a CSV extract of the last 30 days with prompt hashes and token counts (anonymized) — PM me the preferred columns and a secure upload link and I’ll push it to procurement. Also cc'ing procurement@finovate.co on this thread.

Alicia
Head of Product | Finovate Payments
alicia@finovate.co | +1 212-555-0107

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@finovate.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, procurement@finovate.co
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: pricing scenarios & prefix-store hit-rate models

Perfect — thanks for the breakdown, Alicia. That template mix is exactly what we needed. Two quick points and an ask: 

1) Mapping your template mix to hit-rate expectations (quick back-of-envelope):
   - Identity (28%): expect 50–70% prefix hit -> ~30–42% full-response-equivalent
   - Billing & FAQ (42%): expect 25–40% prefix hit -> ~15–24% equivalent
   - Free-text (30%): expect <5% effective hit
   - Weighted blended mid estimate -> ~24% full-response-equivalent (which maps to effective $/1M = $25 * (1 - 0.24) = ~$19.00)

2) For your procurement target ($50 / 1M served) the math is conservative — even without aggressive tuning you should land well under that ceiling at current volumes. The value prop for you is the downside protection during spikes: because hit-rate is measured on request patterns, short bursts don't materially lower the hit-rate on stabilized templates, so the effective $/1M holds for your sustained traffic.

Ask: please upload a CSV with these columns: timestamp, prompt_hash, prompt_template_id (if available), tokens_requested, tokens_generated. If procurement prefers S3, we can provide a pre-signed URL. Once Ben ingests the file we’ll run a sweep and return a hit-rate distribution and a recommended TTL per template.

If agreeable, we’ll also propose a 2-week instrumented PoC that:
- Enables prefix-store for the top 3 templates
- Measures measured hit_rate (prefix and full-equivalent)
- Returns a monthlyized projection and recommended price band for an MSA

Next call? I’m free Mon/Tue afternoon PST for a 30-min sync to align procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@finovate.co>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: pricing scenarios & prefix-store hit-rate models

Looping in operational next steps from my side. Hi Alicia — I’ll take the CSV when it’s ready and run three quick simulations:
1) Baseline parse: dedupe prompt_hash, compute median tokens_requested and tokens_generated per template
2) Synthetic prefix matching: run a sweep of prefix lengths (10, 25, 50 tokens) to estimate hit curves by template class
3) Cost projection: translate simulated hit curves to effective $/1M and monthly spend across your 60M baseline and 120M peak scenario

Deliverables in 72 business hours after ingest:
- Hit-rate distribution chart (CSV + PNG)
- Recommended TTL and prefix length per template class
- Two recommended pricing bands (PoC pilot rate and scaled committed rate) with assumptions called out

I’ll also include a short README and the command I used to simulate the prefix hits so you can reproduce locally. If you’d rather, we can sign an NDA before we take the logs — just let us know procurement’s preference.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
